highlights.title: Quiet, lower week
highlights.text: The ASPI fell 171 points (−0.80%) over the four-day week to 21,198.24 and the S&P SL20 0.60% to 6,039.02. Turnover dropped to Rs 6.6bn from Rs 20.21bn (Rs 1.64bn a day vs Rs 4.04bn); market cap Rs 7,658bn (−0.5%).

highlights.title: Big four banks: mixed 3Q26
highlights.text: HNB Stockbrokers says COMB, HNB, NTB and SAMP grew interest and fee income and improved asset quality, but about Rs 17.8bn of mark-to-market and FX losses cut profits by 24% q/q on average. It expects flat margins for six months and slower loan growth. No targets were given; this site's fair values are COMB Rs 182, HNB Rs 448, SAMP Rs 184.74.

highlights.title: Foreigners sell Dialog
highlights.text: Foreigners were small net sellers for the week (−Rs 53.7mn; bought Rs 305.1mn, sold Rs 358.8mn). Dialog (DIAL.N0000) took almost all the selling, about Rs 0.22bn; HDFC, COMB and HAYL saw the most buying. The site's Dialog fair value is Rs 29.05, below the Rs 47.60 close on 26 Nov.

highlights.title: Momentum runs past fair value
highlights.text: Singer (SING.N0000) more than doubled in ten days. Two shares analysed here are also on the list and well above this site's fair values: Janashakthi Insurance (JINS.N0000, +14.6%; Rs 48.20 on 26 Nov vs fair value Rs 16.06) and PickMe (PKME.N0000, +9.3%; Rs 189.50 vs Rs 83.25).

highlights.title: Tax reliefs cost Rs 780bn
highlights.text: The Finance Ministry's Tax Expenditure Statement puts 2025 VAT and SSCL reliefs at Rs 636bn (a conservative minimum) and customs duty reliefs at Rs 144bn, mostly fuel-duty waivers. Wholesale and retail got the most VAT relief (Rs 188bn).

keyPoints: The big four banks had a mixed 3Q26: net interest income and fee income grew and asset quality improved.
Mark-to-market and foreign-exchange losses of about Rs 17.8bn weighed on results, so profits fell 24% q/q on average.
Loan growth slowed to an average of 4.9% as banks lent more selectively, even though credit demand stayed firm.
forecasts: Net interest margins broadly flat over the next six months
Little loan repricing from the latest 25bps rate hike
Credit growth likely to slow further

news.title: Top PAYE rate threshold to rise above Rs 500,000
news.text: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said the income level at which the top 36% PAYE tax bracket starts will be raised above Rs 500,000, either next year or the year after.

news.title: ADB lends $200mn for small businesses
news.text: Sri Lanka signed a $200mn Asian Development Bank programme to build a stronger, more inclusive financial system for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, the Finance Ministry said.

news.title: World Bank's first Sri Lankan rupee borrowing line
news.text: IFC set up a six-year fixed-rate rupee borrowing line with HSBC Sri Lanka (about $5mn), its first in Asia. With other local funding it backs a $10mn, 10-year rupee loan to one of the country's largest renewable energy companies: IFC's longest rupee loan and first infrastructure investment here since the crisis. Lending in rupees spares borrowers currency risk.

news.title: VAT and SSCL reliefs cost Rs 636bn in 2025
news.text: VAT reliefs rose 25.8% to Rs 419bn and SSCL reliefs were Rs 216bn. Wholesale and retail got Rs 188bn of VAT and Rs 54bn of SSCL relief, electricity and gas Rs 65bn of VAT relief. VAT reliefs were Rs 243bn in the first half of 2026 (+17.2%). The Ministry calls the figures a conservative minimum, as they rest only on filed returns.

news.title: Customs duty reliefs Rs 144bn in 2025
news.text: Import duty reliefs rose 4.4% to Rs 144bn, 91% of it (Rs 131bn) Section 19A waivers, mainly on fuel as petrol and diesel imports rose 5.4% to 2.51mn tonnes; the count now also includes petrol. Animal-feed ingredients got Rs 7.8bn. First-half 2026 reliefs were Rs 74bn.

news.title: ADB: stability alone won't drive the next phase
news.text: ADB's country director said Sri Lanka's recovery is at a turning point where macroeconomic stability is no longer enough; domestic reforms and a push on exports are needed for long-term growth.

news.title: Brent near month's high on Gulf supply fears
news.text: Brent crude futures held near November's high as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi energy facilities raised worries about oil exports from the region.

news.title: Asian shares steady; dollar heads for third monthly gain
news.text: Asian markets were calmer at the end of a rough month as a holiday lull eased AI-related nerves, while the dollar was set for a third monthly rise on safe-haven buying and bets on rate hikes.
